newsitem.title: UK: Fewer UK households expect improved economy - GfK.
newsitem.headline: Fewer UK households expect improved economy - GfK.

text.p: Only 22 percent of British households expect the economic situation to improve in the next year, October's European Commission confidence survey showed.
The survey, conducted by GfK, showed 20 percent of households said the British economy would improve a little while only two percent said it would get a lot better.
In September, 25 percent of households forecast some improvement.
The largest number of households, 38 percent, said the economic situation would stay little changed while 30 percent said it would get either a little, or much worse.
Asked about the economy over the past 12 months, 13 percent of British households said the economy had shown slight improvement. Only one percent said it was much healthier.
Thirty percent saw little change while 52 percent said things had got worse to some degree.

In terms of each household's financial position, 20 percent expected their finances to pick up to some extent over the next year, 56 percent expected little change and 17 percent expected their situation to deteriorate.
